title: Generic-length cycle exact sequence for coherent support categories
statement:
Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a Noetherian finite-type $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Dimensions are Krull dimensions of closed subsets [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For an integer $r\geq0$, let $\mathcal C_r(X)$ be the collection of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent] whose support has dimension at most $r$, with the short exact sequences inherited from module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; set $\mathcal C_{-1}(X)=\{0\}$. Define $K_0(\mathcal C_r(X))$ to be the abelian group on isomorphism classes of its objects, subject to $[\mathcal M]=[\mathcal M']+[\mathcal M'']$ for every such short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal M'\to\mathcal M\to\mathcal M''\to0$. Let $k\geq0$ and let $Z_k(X)$ be the free abelian group on integral closed subschemes $V\subseteq X$ of dimension $k$, where integral means reduced and irreducible. Write $\eta_V$ for the generic point of $V$ and $\mathcal M_{\eta_V}$ for the module stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. For $\mathcal M\in\mathcal C_k(X)$ these stalks have finite length over $\mathcal O_{X,\eta_V}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length], and only finitely many are nonzero. The formula
$$c_k([\mathcal M])=\sum_{V\subseteq X,\ V\ \mathrm{integral\ closed},\ \dim V=k}\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,\eta_V}}(\mathcal M_{\eta_V})[V]$$
defines a homomorphism, and the sequence
$$K_0(\mathcal C_{k-1}(X))\xrightarrow{\iota_k}K_0(\mathcal C_k(X))\xrightarrow{c_k}Z_k(X)\longrightarrow0$$
is exact, with $\iota_k$ induced by inclusion. In particular $\ker c_k=\operatorname{im}\iota_k$.

proof.text: The chain definition gives the following elementary dimension facts. A closed subset of a space of dimension at most $r$ has dimension at most $r$. If $T\subsetneq Z$ is closed and $Z$ is irreducible closed with $\dim Z\leq r$, append $Z$ to any irreducible closed chain in $T$: thus $\dim T\leq r-1$, and $T=\varnothing$ when $r=0$. A finite union of closed sets has dimension their maximum: the largest member of any irreducible closed chain in the union lies in one member of the union, hence so does the whole chain. Stalk exactness gives $\operatorname{Supp}B=\operatorname{Supp}A\cup\operatorname{Supp}C$ for $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$. Thus support bounds pass to subobjects, quotients and extensions.

source.place: Tag 0055 (definition-Krull); chow.tex Tag 02S8 (lemma-Serre-subcategories), the omitted support argument, written out.

proof.text: For a closed immersion $i:Z\to X$ used below, $Z$ is locally Noetherian: its affine chart rings are $R/J$ with $R$ Noetherian, and ideals of $R/J$ are generated by the images of generators of their inverse-image ideals in $R$. The structure module $\mathcal O_Z$ is quasi-coherent of finite type, being free of rank one, hence coherent by the coherent/finite-type criterion. The closed-immersion coherent equivalence makes $i_*\mathcal O_Z$ and $i_*I$ coherent for every coherent ideal $I$ on $Z$. Kernels and cokernels of maps between coherent modules are coherent. The same finite-type criterion and the closed-support theorem show that every coherent module occurring below has closed support. This applies in particular to integral closed subschemes and to all filtration factors below.

Fix $M\in\mathcal C_r(X)$, $r\geq0$. The coherent integral filtration theorem gives $0=M_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq M_m=M$ with $Q_j=M_j/M_{j-1}\cong(i_j)_*I_j$, where $i_j:Z_j\to X$ is an integral closed subscheme and $I_j$ is a nonzero coherent ideal on $Z_j$. Stalk exactness gives $\operatorname{Supp}Q_j\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}M$. In fact $\operatorname{Supp}Q_j=Z_j$: the closed-pushforward stalk formula gives containment in $Z_j$; this support is closed by step 2 and contains the generic point $\eta_j$ since $(I_j)_{\eta_j}=\mathcal O_{Z_j,\eta_j}\neq0$ by the generic-ideal lemma. Taking its closure gives all of $Z_j$. Thus $\dim Z_j\leq r$, and all $M_j,Q_j$ belong to $\mathcal C_r(X)$. This is a finite filtration; for $M=0$ the empty filtration is allowed.

source.place: Tag 01YF (lemma-coherent-filter), combined with the generic-ideal observation used in Tag 01YL (lemma-property-irreducible-higher-rank-cohomological).

proof.text:
Take $r=k$ and integral closed $V$ of dimension $k$. If $(Q_j)_{\eta_V}\neq0$, the stalk formula puts $\eta_V\in Z_j$, hence $V\subseteq Z_j$. Since $\dim Z_j\leq k$, step 1 forces $V=Z_j$ as closed subsets. Both are reduced closed subschemes with this underlying set, so the uniqueness clause (3) of the reduced induced closed subscheme lemma gives them the same ideal sheaf: $V=Z_j$ as closed subschemes, and $(i_j)_*\mathcal O_{Z_j}\cong i_*\mathcal O_V$. For $Z_j=V$, the generic-ideal lemma and the linear closed-pushforward stalk isomorphism identify $(Q_j)_{\eta_V}$ with $\mathcal O_{V,\eta_V}$. This is the residue field of $\mathcal O_{X,\eta_V}$: the closed-immersion stalk map is surjective and its target is a field. Its length over $\mathcal O_{X,\eta_V}$ is one because its only submodules are zero and itself. All other factors have zero stalk. Stalk exactness and length additivity along the finite filtration give
$$\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,\eta_V}}M_{\eta_V}=\#\{j:Z_j=V\}.$$
Thus all these stalks have finite length and only the finitely many dimension-$k$ factors can contribute.

source.place: Tags 02QW (lemma-length-finite), 02QX (definition-cycle-associated-to-coherent-sheaf), 02S9 (lemma-cycles-k-group); algebra.tex Tag 00IV (lemma-length-additive). Finite-filtration version of the generic-length calculation.

proof.text: For a short exact sequence in $\mathcal C_k(X)$, stalk exactness and length additivity give $c_k(B)=c_k(A)+c_k(C)$ coefficient by coefficient. Isomorphisms induce stalk isomorphisms, so the formula respects isomorphism classes and the defining $K_0$ relations and defines a homomorphism. Inclusion of the smaller support category respects the same relations and defines $\iota_k$. If $M\in\mathcal C_{k-1}(X)$, no stalk $M_{\eta_V}$ with $\dim V=k$ can be nonzero, since its closed support would contain $V$; thus $c_k\iota_k=0$. For $k=0$ the smaller category is $\{0\}$, as stipulated. Finally $i_*\mathcal O_V$ is coherent by step 2 and has cycle $[V]$: at $\eta_V$ its stalk is the residue field, while for an integral closed $V'$ of dimension $k$ with $\eta_{V'}\in V$ one has $V'\subseteq V$, hence $V'=V$ as closed subsets by step 1 and as closed subschemes by the uniqueness clause (3) of the reduced induced closed subscheme lemma; so every other basis element has zero coefficient. Hence $c_k$ is surjective.

For a factor $Q_j=i_*I_j$ with $\dim Z_j=k$, consider $i_*I_j\to i_*\mathcal O_{Z_j}$. It is injective on stalks by the closed-pushforward stalk formula and the injectivity of $I_j\to\mathcal O_{Z_j}$, hence is a monomorphism by stalk exactness. Its cokernel $T_j$ is coherent by step 2. Its support is closed, contained in $Z_j$, and misses $\eta_j$ since $(I_j)_{\eta_j}=\mathcal O_{Z_j,\eta_j}$. Step 1 gives $\dim\operatorname{Supp}T_j\leq k-1$. If $k=0$ the support is empty and $T_j=0$: every section is locally zero because its germs are zero. The short exact sequence gives $[Q_j]=[i_*\mathcal O_{Z_j}]-[T_j]$ in $K_0(\mathcal C_k(X))$. If $\dim Z_j<k$, the factor $Q_j$ itself belongs to $\mathcal C_{k-1}(X)$ and its class already lies in $\operatorname{im}\iota_k$.

source.place: Tag 02S9 (lemma-cycles-k-group), final two short exact sequences; here specialized to ideal factors already supplied by coherent.tex Tag 01YF.

proof.text: Define $s:Z_k(X)\to K_0(\mathcal C_k(X))$ by $s([V])=[i_*\mathcal O_V]$ on the free basis. Telescope the filtration relations to obtain $[M]=\sum_j[Q_j]$. Replace the dimension-$k$ factors using step 6; all remaining terms are images of smaller-support coherent classes. Step 4 counts the multiplicity of each $V$ among those factors. Therefore $[M]-s(c_k([M]))\in\operatorname{im}\iota_k$. Both maps are homomorphisms, so the assertion extends to every integral linear combination $x$ of object classes, hence every $x\in K_0(\mathcal C_k(X))$. If $c_k(x)=0$ it gives $x\in\operatorname{im}\iota_k$. The reverse inclusion is step 5. Together with surjectivity this proves the stated exact sequence, including empty $X$, no dimension-$k$ subvarieties, and $k=0$.
